explain.say: Why does some music sound sunny and bright, and other music sound sad or spooky? A big part of the answer is the scale, a ladder of notes going up. Let us climb the C major scale on a piano, using only white keys. Look at the first step: C to D, a tone, which means a whole step.

explain.say: Climb on: D to E is another tone. Now look at the third step, E to F. On a piano there is no black key between them, so they are next-door neighbours: a semitone, which means a half step. Can you find the other place on the white keys with no black key between?

explain.say: Brilliant climbing! Every major scale follows that same pattern, starting on any note. Wow fact: change just one note, E down to E flat, and C major turns sad. Challenge: play C, E, G and then C, E flat, G, and listen for happy and sad.

faq.a: A major scale is a set of eight notes going up with the pattern tone, tone, semitone, tone, tone, tone, semitone. C major uses only the white keys from C to C, and major scales sound bright.
asks: What is the pattern of a major scale?

faq.a: A semitone, or half step, is the smallest step on a piano: from one key to the very next key, black or white, like E to F or B to C.
asks: Why are E and F next to each other?

faq.q: What is a tone in music?
faq.a: A tone, or whole step, is two semitones: it skips one key on the piano, like C to D, which skips the black key between them.

faq.q: Why do minor keys sound sad?
faq.a: The minor scale has a lower third note, and some other lowered notes, which our ears often hear as darker or sadder. How sad it sounds also depends on culture, speed and how it is played.
A natural minor is the scale from A to A using only white keys: A, B, C, D, E, F, G, A. It shares its notes with C major but starts in a different place.
asks: What is the relative minor of C?
Which minor uses only white keys?

facts: The major scale follows the pattern tone, tone, semitone, tone, tone, tone, semitone.
A natural minor and C major use the same seven notes, so A minor is called the relative minor of C major.

quiz.say: Which pair of white keys is a semitone apart?
quiz.why: There is no black key between E and F, so they are a half step apart.

wrong.1: C to D has a black key between, so it is a whole tone.
wrong.2: F to G has a black key between, so it is a whole tone.

quiz.say: You want a melody to sound sad. Which scale would most composers choose?
quiz.why: The lower third and other lowered notes of minor scales tend to sound sad or serious.

wrong.1: Major scales usually sound bright and happy.
